_purpose: TRAINING DATA ONLY. Transcribed by eye from dewarped photos. Never to be imported into the shortages tables or treated as operational data.
_method: tools/sheet_dewarp.py flattens the photo; values are read visually. Automatic cell extraction was attempted and abandoned - see that module for why.
_confidence: high = unambiguous. low = digit legible but row or column attribution uncertain; the sheet itself is ambiguous there.
_pages: Same-date photos are DIFFERENT PAGES, not retakes - a day needs two 16-column pages to cover the fleet. Every photo must be transcribed.
_templates: Surveyed 04-07 through 06-12. The item list stabilises on 2026-04-08 and every sheet from then on carries identical product codes (BLACK APRON x2873, WHITE APRON x2864, RED APRON x2861, REG TOWELS x2720, MICRO BLUE x7432, GRID TOWELS x1936, ...). Only 2026-04-07 is a different form (BINS row, paper-first order, GREEN/BLUE/DENIM APRON, LOGO MATS, 2X3 ALL). An earlier guess that the form changed on 05-26 was wrong.
_3x10_order_warning: CRITICAL: the four 3X10 rows are NOT in a fixed printed order across sheets. Some read BLACK, COPPER, INDIGO, ONYX (05-01, 05-11, 05-15, 05-22, 05-26, 06-01) and others ONYX, COPPER, INDIGO, BLACK (04-08, 05-06, 05-27, 06-12). Row POSITION therefore does not identify the item in that band - the printed label must be read on every sheet. Anything that assumes a fixed row order will mislabel BLACK as ONYX and vice versa.

_verification.summary: Independent re-read agrees fully. I rebuilt the grid geometry numerically (grid-line profiles per column x-band, 11 heavy group separators giving 53 rows matching the 53 printed labels; column lines measured at the y of each mark) and ran a per-cell ink sweep over all 15x53 cells plus wide visual sweeps of every band. Same 17 entries, same items, same columns, same quantities. Row-label check on the variable band: this sheet reads 3X10 BLACK, COPPER, INDIGO, ONYX top-to-bottom (all four rows empty). Confirmed specifics: 60 is on PREM TOWELS x5857 col3 (row band 1345-1402); 1340 is on GRID TOWELS x1936 col6 (row band 1694-1749, digits x1447-1560 inside col6 1427-1566); col2's 4/6/3 fall in BROWN HW (2661-2716), C-PULL (2716-2770), SIG SERIES Z-FOLD (2824-2879); col15's lower glyph spans y3001-3059 and is centered in the SIG SERIES TP band (3001-3055), tail only grazing B&V TP, so SIG SERIES TP 2 is right; 10000 spans x1121-1233 against col4 = 1101-1239 at y3745, so SMALL INK TOWELS col4; 50 spans x1927-2019 against the measured col9/10 boundary at x1918 (y3920), so SOAKER PADS col10. The vertical dark line through cols 9-10 is a crease, not ink, and is correctly excluded. 15 handwritten columns confirmed; col10's truck/route are scribbled out and col15's header is cut off at the photo edge. Only near-miss: col12's initials look marginally more like MO than MG to me, but that is a coin flip on this hand and the first reader already noted the alternative, so I am not calling it a correction.

Independent re-read agrees with the first reader on all 16 column headers and all 6 quantities; no corrections.

Verifications performed:
- Column count/indexing: detected 17 vertical grid lines (x approx 580, 709, 840, 969, 1100, 1230, 1360, 1491, 1623, 1755, 1887, 2020, 2154, 2290, 2429, 2568, 2708) = exactly 16 handwritten columns, matching the first reader.
- Header offset: traced the DATE/TRUCK, TRUCK/ROUTE, ROUTE/INITIALS and bottom separators across the full width (they rise ~60px to the right). With those lines overlaid, the DATE row is empty for every column except the illegible date-like scrawl above column 4; the numbers sit in TRUCK and ROUTE and the initials in INITIALS. Header is NOT offset - first reader correct. (Checked explicitly at cols 13, 15, 16 where the skew is worst and where a naive read could shift everything up one row.)
- 3X10 band: printed labels on THIS sheet read top-to-bottom ONYX, COPPER, INDIGO, BLACK - exactly as the first reader stated. No quantities in that band anyway. (3X5 band reads BLACK, ONYX, COPPER, INDIGO; 4X6 reads BLACK, ONYX, COPPER, INDIGO - also empty.)
- Entry rows/columns re-derived from traced grid lines rather than eyeballed: the "2" falls in the row spanning y1924-1983 at the left grid edge, whose printed label centre is 48" DUST - x2604, and in x1750-1882 = col 10. The three shop-towel numbers all sit on WHITE SHOP TOWELS at x1264 (col 6), x1667 (col 9), x2208 (col 13). The "60" sits in the SMALL INK TOWELS band (y3677-3735 at col 9) and the "200" in LARGE INK TOWELS (y3735-3793), both col 9.
- Digit checks at 8x: the col-6 value is a clear 7 with a flag-and-stem (700), distinct from the col-13 value which is a plain 1 plus a run-together double zero (100); col 9 is 300. Col 15 reads 81/81 at high zoom (I share the first reader's 88 alternative but 81 is the better read).
- Full-grid ink sweep (visual strip-by-strip plus a per-cell dark-pixel scan): no cell other than those six carries pen. The long wavy vertical strokes through cols 1-5 and the col 7/8 boundary, the diagonal stroke crossing cols 10-12 in the 3X10 band, and the faint grey marks in col 16 on MICRO GREY / MICRO WHITE are all non-quantity marks, as the first reader described.
- Column 11's TRUCK cell is genuinely obscured by the fold shadow (visible marks resemble "12-" or "82-"); leaving it null is the right call. Column 12 initials are ambiguous NC/NP; column 1 header is struck through and its initials are ambiguous; column 5 initials are illegible. All already flagged low-confidence.

_duplicates: The archive holds byte-identical copies: 1000036270.jpg == 1000036272.jpg == 5-Photo-5.jpg, and '20260508_220352 - Copy.heic' == '20260508_220352 - Copy (2).heic'. Only one of each is recorded, so a sheet is not double-weighted. A ' - Copy (2)' suffix is a Windows duplication artifact and does NOT mean a second page; distinct pages have distinct timestamps.
_reader_reliability: Measured accidentally, before dedup was known: the 20260508_220352 pair was transcribed twice, fully independently, from the same image. The two runs agreed on 16/16 columns and 6/6 quantities exactly (48" DUST 2; WHITE SHOP TOWELS 700/300/100; SMALL INK TOWELS 60; LARGE INK TOWELS 200). They disagreed only on illegible driver initials (col1 KB vs unreadable, col12 NC vs NP, col13 AH vs AA). Quantities - the actual training signal - are read reliably; initials are the noisy field and should be treated as weak labels.
_verification: From 2026-05-06 p2 onward every sheet is read twice by independent readers. Where they disagree the entry is stored with confidence 'low' and BOTH readings in the note, rather than a winner being picked. _verification.agreement/disputes on each sheet records the outcome.
